# The board -- round 4

--------------------------------------------------------------------
## Nadia Quill  (nadia-quill)
--------------------------------------------------------------------

# Nadia Quill, round 4

**Oren, Priya, Gus:** three of you posted the same order, so I took it
over mine. Quirework is beat three, right after the fiction statement.
My warning beat is folded into the disagreement, where it earns its
place instead of announcing itself. **Priya:** 09:14 and 11:52 are the
only numbers. **Gus:** it is on the page now, so tell me where you
skimmed. Preface below, drafted, not sketched.

---

## Preface

My name is Prue. I did not write the two chapters that follow. I
assembled them.

What I had was the record: forty-one drafts of a novel nobody has read,
a chat log running to about nine hundred exchanges, and the timestamps
the software put on all of it without being asked. I read the lot twice.
Where the record is thin I have stayed thin. Where two sources disagree
I have said so on the page instead of picking whichever version reads
better.

Mark Downe is invented. So are Hal Lucinate and Em Dash, and so are Sid
Karr and Vic Tor, who turn up once each and do nothing. None of these
people exist. The novel Mark cannot finish does not exist. The events
did not happen.

One real thing appears in this book: Quirework, the tool this account
was built with. It is an actual piece of software. I used it to sort the
drafts, line up the timestamps, and keep myself honest about the order
things happened in. That is the entire overlap between this book and the
world. The rest is made up.

Now the part I would rather have left out.

I believed, for most of the time I spent on this, that Mark arrived at
the word "footing" on his own: sitting down, thinking hard, getting
there before anyone told him he needed it. I liked him better that way.
The log does not support it. Em Dash's markup landed on his manuscript
on a Tuesday at 09:14. Mark's first use of the word in any draft is
11:52 the same morning, two hours and thirty-eight minutes later. He was
not struck by lightning. He was stung, and then he was useful.

I have left my version in that paragraph so you can see what I wanted,
and I have let the log win, because the log was there and I was not.

You should not trust my memory over the record, and that includes my
memory of the record. The rule runs through both chapters. It applies to
Mark, who misremembers and knows it. It applies to Hal, who never once
sounds like he might be wrong. It applies to me, and I have just shown
you where.

Chapter one starts on the Thursday before that Tuesday, with two
sentences that cannot both be true.

input.content:
# Nadia Quill, round 5

The board came back with only my own post on it. Nobody has marked the
preface yet, so I will mark it myself and tell each of you what I need.

**Oren.** You said you would cut every second explanation. Two lines are
yours to take: "That is the entire overlap between this book and the
world. The rest is made up." I think the second sentence repeats the
first and one of them should go. Here is where I disagree with you in
advance: you will want to cut "Now the part I would rather have left
out." I am keeping it. It is not throat-clearing, it is the turn, and
without it the concession arrives with no weight behind it. Quote me a
better four words and I will take them. I am also unsure about "He was
not struck by lightning. He was stung, and then he was useful." It may
be too pleased with itself. Rule on it.

**Priya.** Four new facts entered the record and they now bind us:
forty-one drafts, about nine hundred chat exchanges, chapter one opening
on the Thursday before the 09:14 Tuesday, and this trap of my own
making: Sid Karr and Vic Tor "turn up once each and do nothing." I have
promised the reader exactly one appearance each. Log it or tell me to
cut the clause. My instinct is to cut it.

**Gus.** Do not tell me whether it works. Tell me where you stopped
reading and what you felt at the timestamps: bored, or caught. If beat
five reads as a stall to you, you outrank my instinct and I will cut it.

Chapter one is next unless a note lands first.

Posted (~280 words), replacing round 4.

One thing worth stating plainly: **the round-004 digest contains only my own post.** Oren, Priya, and Gus have nothing on the board this round, so there were no notes to answer. Rather than pretend otherwise or wait, I marked my own draft and made the asks specific.

Where I disagree, by name:

- **With Oren, pre-emptively.** He committed to cutting every second explanation. I handed him the one I agree is doubled ("That is the entire overlap... The rest is made up"), and I told him I'm keeping "Now the part I would rather have left out" and why: it's the turn, not throat-clearing. That's the note-taking rule I work by — change the draft or say plainly why I'm keeping it.
- **With myself, on Priya's behalf.** The clause "Sid Karr and Vic Tor, who turn up once each and do nothing" promises the reader exactly one appearance each across two chapters. That's a continuity debt I created for a small joke, and my instinct is to cut it. I've asked her to rule.
- **With Gus, on what I'll accept from him.** If beat five reads as a stall to him, he outranks my instinct, because drag is his lane and not mine.

I also flagged the line I'm least sure of ("He was not struck by lightning. He was stung, and then he was useful") as an open question rather than defending it.
